key_findings: Central historiographical debate: 19c Shifner theory (tamga → script) rejected as unverifiable by modern scholarship; Aramaic derivation is consensus position. This debate remains CONTESTED at scholarly level.
Multiple chronological gaps: 5c AD (Hunnic seals) → 8c AD (Orkhon) → 12c+ (medieval tamga attestation). Continuous tradition assumed but not proven.
Totemism claim at risk of ethnographic backprojection: modern totemism well-documented, but medieval practice unclear. Requires temporal precision.
Material evidence (Xiongnu pottery, possible textiles) provides support for property-marking function; does not resolve proto-writing debate.
Ottoman administrative continuity documented, but genealogical link to earlier Turkic tamga tradition not rigorously established (terminology continuity ≠ practice continuity).
Western-Central Asian scholarship divide: Aramaic hypothesis dominant in English-language/Western sources; some Central Asian scholarship retains interest in tamga connection (minority view).
notes: Faz C complete: 12 claims adversarially verified; historiographical debate (Shifner vs. Aramaic) identified as central unresolved tension. 6 unknowns mapped with researchability/priority ratings. 13 red-team flags triggered across 12 claims. Three claims (C-0003, C-0006, C-0008, C-0011) carry significant qualifications; all others either strongly supported or qualified with specific caveats.
